notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS exploring Redwood for relevance/reranking. Primary drive is improve product recommendation ordering + session re-ranking for search. Team: Head of Product (Claire H.), Sr. ML Engineer (Marco L.), Platform Eng (Priya N.).

POC plan: start with Hosted API for rapid iteration on rerank endpoint (batch offline scoring + live candidate re-rank). If POC meets latency/cost targets, move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation. They explicitly asked for an offline scoring path (bulk rerank of candidate lists) to integrate into nightly pipelines.

Requirements (from call):
- Use-case: reranking of candidate lists produced by current retrieval pipeline; offline scoring for A/B test and regression evaluation.
- Eval set: planning ~100k query-candidate pairs for initial offline run (we currently have 48k prepared; they will add 50k more).
- Metrics: MRR and NDCG primary; precision@5 secondary. Want help mapping Redwood eval hooks to their metrics.
- Latency/throughput: target P95 <= 150-200ms on production rerank calls; expected steady-state QPS ~10 but bursty during peak indexing runs.
- Cost sensitivity: mid; willing to commit to dedicated capacity if unit cost predictable and caching reduces token spend.
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2 evidence, audit logs, KMS integration for any private keys, and EU data residency for a subset of customer data.

Customer quotes (paraphrased):
- "Need guarantee on P95 below 200ms for the rerank API or we can't route live traffic"
- "If we can get predictable unit cost we'll commit to a 12-month reserved pool"

Technical notes from SE (Samir):
- Discussed prefix/KV caching, continuous batching tradeoffs, and fallback to smaller model variant when Dedicated pool saturated.
- Marco asked for an offline scoring example (Python notebook) that uses the rerank endpoint to score large candidate sets — we promised a sample Jupyter with pagination and checkpointing.

Commercial/Procurement:
- They prefer starting host-pay-as-you-go for POC (hosted_api). Pricing conversation now focused on committed tier pricing for Dedicated once POC succeeds. Procurement cycle ~4-6 weeks after POC sign-off.

Next steps (explicit):
- Send SOC2 report + security FAQ (AE) — target 2026-03-12.
- Provide test keys for staged hosted POC + sample Jupyter offline scoring notebook (SE) — target 2026-03-15.
- Run first offline scoring pass on 50k candidate pairs; share NDCG baseline (joint AE/SE) — target 2026-03-22.
- Pricing follow-up: provide committed vs payg scenarios and an estimated cost-per-rerank (pricing deck link).

Other notes: they mentioned evaluating Algolia and Pinecone for vector + ranker composition. Primary differentiator for Redwood is the unified inference (hosted -> dedicated) and observability (per-route token & latency breakdown). Keep follow-ups short and technical; product team wants concrete examples and reproducible evals.
